headline: Wizz Air flight from Luton diverted to Budapest after bomb threat: See full details
subheadline: London-Sofia Wizz Air flight makes emergency landing in Hungary
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A Wizz Air flight travelling from London Luton Airport to Sofia was forced to make an emergency landing in Budapest on Monday, November 2, after receiving a bomb threat mid-flight, with a Hungarian fighter jet to escort the aircraft.

Wizz Air flight 4302 departed Luton at 08:33 GMT and was due to arrive in the Bulgarian capital at 13:25 local time. According to flight-tracking data, the Airbus A321 neo was flying over Bosnia and Herzegovina when it changed course and headed north towards Hungary, landing at Budapest Liszt Ferenc International Airport at 12:09 local time.

Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi confirmed that a Gripen fighter jet from the Hungarian Defence Forces took to the skies “within minutes” to provide an escort for the passenger aircraft, before returning to its base at Kecskemet.

Control over the situation was handed over to the police on the ground.

According to the statement issued by Wizz Air, "the aircraft landed safely at Budapest Liszt Ferenc International Airport in compliance with the relevant security protocols and procedures, before taxiing to a stand, where the necessary security check was performed on the aircraft and the passengers."

Wizz Air clarified later that the "security check was completed and nothing was found." It was also mentioned that the aircraft would take off very soon in order to proceed to Sofia. Wizz Air assured the people that it is "fully cooperating with the authorities" and "safety of our passengers and crew remains our highest priority."

It is still not clear who made the threat or whether it was made onboard or on the ground. This incident has come at a time when there have been a number of threats in the world of aviation in the past few months, one of them being the hijack threat to a Flydubai flight in September.

headline: 'We're going to crash': Learjet crew's terrifying final 35 seconds captured on audio
subheadline: Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft's descent rate briefly exceeded 32,000 feet per minute
author: Web Desk
article_text:
“We're out of time.” Those were the final words heard from the cockpit of a private jet that crashed in Florida, killing all nine people aboard, as newly released audio revealed the crew's desperate attempts to save the aircraft in its final seconds.

The recording, obtained from air traffic control communications, captured the Learjet 60 crew initially reporting ice accumulation and moderate turbulence while flying towards the Bahamas on Sunday, November 1.

At first, the situation appeared manageable. The crew told controllers they were dealing with the ice but needed smoother flying conditions.

Less than a minute later, the routine conversation turned into an emergency.

"Mayday, mayday," a crew member radioed, warning that the aircraft was descending at 10,000 feet per minute.

Seconds later, the reported descent rate doubled to 20,000 feet per minute as the jet continued losing altitude.

"We're going to crash into the ground," the crew warned.

An air traffic controller attempted to maintain contact, telling the pilots: "I'm here with you. Talk to me."

The crew then reported descending at 22,000 feet per minute, with the aircraft banking sharply.

In the final moments, a voice reportedly shouted for someone named Jack to look outside before the transmission ended with the words: "We're out of time."

The exchange unfolded in roughly 35 seconds, according to Reuters.

Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft's descent rate briefly exceeded 32,000 feet per minute before it struck a residential area in Palm Beach County and exploded.

The jet had departed Austin, Texas, and was heading to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas.

The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the crash. Although the crew reported icing and turbulence, investigators have not established what caused the aircraft to lose control.

headline: Pakistani-Americans among candidates in US state elections
subheadline: Candidates contest seats in Connecticut, Texas, Georgia, Pennsylvania, Nevada and Florida
author: Sibt-e-Arif
article_text:
Pakistani-Americans are contesting elections in several US states ahead of the midterm elections on November 3, 2026, with some seeking re-election to their state legislatures.

According to available election lists, Maryam Khan and Saud Anwar are contesting seats in the Connecticut State Senate. In Texas, Salman Bhojani and Suleman Lalani are seeking re-election to the State House of Representatives from Districts 92 and 76, respectively.

Farooq Mughal is contesting a state legislative seat in Georgia, while Tariq Khan is running in Pennsylvania. Hanadi Nadeem is also seeking a seat in the Nevada State Assembly.

In Florida, Imtiaz Mohammad is standing as a Republican candidate. Several other Muslim American candidates are also contesting elections in various states.

Most of the Pakistani-American candidates are running for seats in state legislatures or state senates. These are state-level elections and should not be confused with contests for the US Congress, which comprises the federal House of Representatives and the Senate.

headline: Man who left home at 29 returns at 57 after walking 31,000 miles around world
subheadline: Karl Bushby was also detained in Panama, Russia and held at gunpoint in Mexico
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A British adventurer who left home as a young man in 1998 has finally returned to his mother's doorstep after spending 28 years travelling around the world without using any transport to move forward.

Karl Bushby, now 57, was welcomed by hundreds of cheering supporters in his hometown of Hull on Monday (November 2), bringing an end to an extraordinary 31,000-mile journey across four continents and 30 countries.

His mother, Angela, broke down in tears as she embraced her son outside the family home, which had been decorated with a banner reading "Welcome Home Son".

"Where have you been?" she jokingly asked him.

Bushby was just 29 when he set off from Chile on November 1, 1998, carrying a tent, a few hundred dollars and a camera.

The former British paratrooper had initially expected the expedition to take around five years. Instead, it consumed nearly half his life.

During the journey, he survived dangerous jungles, crossed the frozen Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia, and spent 31 days swimming across the Caspian Sea.

He was also detained in Panama and Russia, held at gunpoint in Mexico and repeatedly delayed by visa restrictions, financial problems and the COVID-19 pandemic.

Bushby revealed that he spent only about 15 of those 28 years actually walking, with the remaining time consumed by paperwork, logistics and securing funding.

His final challenge came last month when he swam across the English Channel to complete the journey without taking a boat or plane.

Back home, his 36-year-old son and 12-year-old granddaughter, whom he had never met, were waiting to welcome him.

Reflecting on the journey, Bushby credited strangers across the world for helping him survive.

"I didn't do this alone," he told supporters, describing the expedition as a global effort.

article_html:
A British adventurer who left home as a young man in 1998 has finally returned to his mother's doorstep after spending 28 years travelling around the world without using any transport to move forward.

Karl Bushby, now 57, was welcomed by hundreds of cheering supporters in his hometown of Hull on Monday (November 2), bringing an end to an extraordinary 31,000-mile journey across four continents and 30 countries.

His mother, Angela, broke down in tears as she embraced her son outside the family home, which had been decorated with a banner reading "Welcome Home Son".

"Where have you been?" she jokingly asked him.

Bushby was just 29 when he set off from Chile on November 1, 1998, carrying a tent, a few hundred dollars and a camera.

The former British paratrooper had initially expected the expedition to take around five years. Instead, it consumed nearly half his life.

During the journey, he survived dangerous jungles, crossed the frozen Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia, and spent 31 days swimming across the Caspian Sea.

He was also detained in Panama and Russia, held at gunpoint in Mexico and repeatedly delayed by visa restrictions, financial problems and the COVID-19 pandemic.

Bushby revealed that he spent only about 15 of those 28 years actually walking, with the remaining time consumed by paperwork, logistics and securing funding.

His final challenge came last month when he swam across the English Channel to complete the journey without taking a boat or plane.

Back home, his 36-year-old son and 12-year-old granddaughter, whom he had never met, were waiting to welcome him.

Reflecting on the journey, Bushby credited strangers across the world for helping him survive.

"I didn't do this alone," he told supporters, describing the expedition as a global effort.

headline: Zayn Malik transforms into Jim Carrey's 'The Mask' character for Halloween
subheadline: The former One Direction star, 33, sports a prosthetic green mask along with the iconic yellow suit
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Zayn Malik has a ssssmokin’ Halloween costume this year.

The former One Direction star dressed up as Jim Carrey’s The Mask character, complete with a prosthetic green mask and the iconic yellow suit, unveiling his look in a series of Instagram posts on Sunday, November 1.

Malik, 33, also shared a behind-the-scenes video documenting the lengthy makeup process, which was handled by Gotham FX and RBFX Makeup Gallery.

READ MORE: Jim Carrey reacts to 'The Mask' director Chuck Russell's death

Fully embracing the character, the singer showed off a range of impressions, channelling everyone from The Terminator and Johnny Bravo to John Lennon and Hermione Granger.

“Shombody shtop mehhh,” he captioned the post, referencing one of the most memorable lines from the 1994 comedy, which also marked Cameron Diaz’s feature film debut.

The Mask follows Stanley Ipkiss (Carrey), a timid bank clerk who discovers a magical wooden mask connected to Loki, the Norse god of mischief. Once he puts it on, he transforms into a chaotic, green-faced trickster with reality-bending powers.

Malik’s Halloween reveal comes shortly after the conclusion of his Konnakol Tour, which supported his fifth studio album of the same name. The nine-date run began in London on May 23 and wrapped up in Lima, Peru, on October 14. The tour was originally scheduled to feature 32 shows, but the US leg, an Irish concert and two UK dates were cancelled due to the singer’s health issues.

READ MORE: Zayn Malik cancels US leg of tour one month after hospitalisation

headline: Four NASA volunteers see outside world after 378 days of living on 'Mars'
subheadline: The four-member crew included commander Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, Matthew Montgomery and James Spicer
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Four volunteers who spent more than a year pretending to live on Mars have finally stepped outside their isolated habitat, seeing the outside world for the first time in 378 days.

The crew emerged from NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston on Saturday (October 31), ending an experiment designed to find out whether humans can survive the isolation, limited supplies and psychological pressures of a journey to the Red Planet.

For more than a year, the volunteers lived inside a 1,700-square-foot, 3D-printed habitat, where they grew crops, conducted simulated spacewalks and carried out scientific experiments.

They also had to communicate with the outside world through artificial delays, recreating the time it takes for messages to travel between Earth and Mars.

Even conversations with family members were restricted to emails delayed to mimic communication across millions of miles.

The four-member crew included commander Ross Elder, medical officer Ellen Ellis, science officer Matthew Montgomery and flight engineer James Spicer.

Speaking after emerging from isolation, Ellis described the experience as a year spent voluntarily cut off from the outside world.

The experiment, known as Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA), began on October 19, 2025.

Throughout the mission, NASA monitored how the volunteers managed their daily routines, physical health, teamwork and limited resources.

The crew will now undergo two weeks of medical evaluations and debriefings to help researchers understand how astronauts might cope with prolonged missions away from Earth.

This was NASA's second year-long Mars simulation, following a similar experiment completed in 2024.

The agency hopes the findings will help prepare astronauts for future missions to the Moon and eventually Mars, where crews could spend years away from home with little possibility of immediate assistance.

headline: Jessica Alba rushes to delete Halloween post after backlash over costume
subheadline: The actress, 45, recreates the brutal 1994 attack on Tonya Harding's figure skating rival Nancy Kerrigan
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Jessica Alba has sparked backlash over her Halloween costume.

According to the Daily Express, the actress dressed up as a battered Nancy Kerrigan with her friend as Tonya Harding, recreating one of sports’ most horrific moments. She has since appeared to have deleted her Instagram post showing off the costume.

Alba, 45, dressed as Kerrigan, 57, in a white outfit, ice skates and a bloodstained bandage around her knee. Her friend Kelly Sawyer dressed as Kerrigan’s rival, Tonya Harding, wearing a sparkly maroon ensemble and posing with a baseball bat.

The costumes were a reference to the 1994 incident in which Kerrigan was attacked with a police baton by Shane Stant, who was hired by Harding’s ex-husband. The assault happened shortly before Olympic qualifiers, forcing Kerrigan to withdraw. Harding was never criminally convicted over the attack but received a lifetime ban from the U.S. Figure Skating Association.

READ MORE: Jessica Alba enjoys 'out of this world' moment with Artemis II mission

The costume choice drew criticism from Alba’s followers, with one commenting, “Immature. We expect better, Jessica.” Another questioned the decision to revisit a traumatic incident, while a third wrote, “Wow, first Martha and now Jessica. Why are we being nasty this Halloween?”

Alba’s deleted post also featured her 8-year-old son Hayes dressed as a vampire. Her daughters, Honor, 18, and Haven, 15, celebrated Halloween too, with Haven sharing her unicorn costume online. Alba has been dating actor Danny Ramirez since separating from ex-husband Cash Warren last year.

READ MORE: Martha Stewart addresses backlash over her Halloween costume

headline: Scientists challenge long-held theory about how life began on Earth
subheadline: The possibility of comets delivering the necessary ingredients could not be ruled out entirely
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Scientists have raised fresh doubts on a popular theory that suggests some of the building blocks of life on Earth were brought here by comets, after they discovered that such cosmic objects could have wiped them out when they crashed into the planet billions of years ago.

For years, scientists have speculated that comets could have delivered organic compounds to the early Earth that contributed to the evolution of life.

But a new study by researchers at the University of Cambridge suggests that the theory has a major problem: the comets may have been travelling too fast for those chemicals to survive the impact.

The findings, published in Scientific Reports, are based on 100,000 computer simulations examining what happens when comets collide with a planet.

Researchers focused on compounds such as hydrogen cyanide, which can play an important role in the chemical reactions that produce amino acids, the building blocks of proteins.

Their calculations suggest that the extreme heat and pressure generated during most comet impacts would have destroyed these fragile compounds before they could contribute to the emergence of life.

Lead researcher Richard Anslow said the possibility of comets delivering the necessary ingredients could not be ruled out entirely, although it would have required unusually favourable circumstances.

The findings also raise questions about whether Mars might have been better placed to receive such chemicals, given differences in the conditions under which comets strike the two planets.

Scientists are now considering whether asteroids played a bigger role in delivering organic material to Earth, or whether the ingredients for life formed here through natural chemical processes.

The study does not explain how life began. It does, however, cast doubt on one proposed route by which some of its essential ingredients may have arrived.

headline: Vivienne Jolie-Pitt legally drops 'Pitt' from her last name
subheadline: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt’s daughter Vivienne officially becomes Vivienne Jolie
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Vivienne Jolie-Pitt, the 18-year-old daughter of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt, has legally dropped “Pitt” from her last name.

The change was approved on Monday 2 November at a hearing in a Los Angeles courtroom.

Her name is now Vivienne Marcheline Jolie, rather than Vivienne Marcheline Jolie-Pitt. She has used “Jolie” as a professional name for more than two years.

Read more: Angelina Jolie fights Brad Pitt over new court demand

Vivienne filed in July to drop her father’s surname, citing “personal” reasons, according to Page Six.

Her attorney, Peter Kenneth Levine, appeared remotely, and Judge Virginia Keeny read out the names of the approved petitions, including hers.

The decree is expected in about a week from room 112 at the Stanley Mosk Courthouse.

Vivienne was first listed as “Vivienne Jolie” in the May 2024 Broadway Playbill for The Outsiders, on which she worked as a producer’s assistant.

Her mother was a producer on the musical.

She is the latest of the couple’s children to move away from the surname. Her twin, Knox, left it off his June 2026 high school graduation certificate, though he has not yet changed it legally.

Shiloh, 20, legally became Shiloh Jolie in August 2024, shortly after turning 18. Maddox, 25, and Zahara, 21, legally dropped the name earlier this year. Pax, 22, is the only sibling still using Pitt.

Brad Pitt has not commented publicly.

In a September interview with L’Officiel, Angelina Jolie said of her children: “They’re definitely individuals.” She added that a key parental goal is “to basically not get in their way.”

headline: Who was Nathalia Filgueiras? Everything to know about 20-year-old Learjet60 copilot killed in Florida
subheadline: Nathalia Filgueiras, 20, Identified as Co-Pilot in Fatal Florida Learjet Crash
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The co-pilot of the Learjet 60 aircraft which crashed and claimed nine lives in Palm Beach County, Florida, on Sunday has been identified as Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, an aspiring commercial pilot who obtained her private pilot’s license even before finishing high school at the age of 20.

According to the information released by Filgueiras’ mother and stepfather, Camila and Thiago Corteleti, to the New York Post, the young pilot, who was born and raised in Boca Raton, had clocked over 1,300 flight hours as well as working for Upper Jets – a privately owned airline based in Fort Lauderdale – as a commercial pilot for the last nine months.

The Learjet was flying from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas when it suddenly descended sharply, falling over 20,000 feet per minute and slamming into the ground near Greenacres, creating a crater from which smoke was seen rising. Disturbing air traffic control recording reveals how the pilot called out “Mayday” and then said, “We're going to crash into the ground.”

Filgueiras had texted her boyfriend only ten minutes prior to the incident, telling him that she was facing turbulence and icing, as per her stepfather. "I wanted her to fulfil her dream, but I understood very well that her dream was the thing that would make her leave me," her mother said. "I know she was following her dream."

Filgueiras hit the local news headlines in 2023 after she received a pilot's license when she was 17 years old, even before she got her driver's license.

Her education was financed by the School District of Palm Beach County's Aviation Academy. "I definitely do brag because people tell me, 'Oh, you can't drive,' and I say to them, 'Yes, I can drive, but I can fly as well,'" she said in an interview with CBS12.

No identity of the remaining eight victims has been released by the authorities yet. An investigation into the reason behind the crash is being conducted by the FAA and the NTSB.

The co-pilot of the Learjet 60 aircraft which crashed and claimed nine lives in Palm Beach County, Florida, on Sunday has been identified as Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, an aspiring commercial pilot who obtained her private pilot’s license even before finishing high school at the age of 20.

According to the information released by Filgueiras’ mother and stepfather, Camila and Thiago Corteleti, to the New York Post, the young pilot, who was born and raised in Boca Raton, had clocked over 1,300 flight hours as well as working for Upper Jets – a privately owned airline based in Fort Lauderdale – as a commercial pilot for the last nine months.

The Learjet was flying from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas when it suddenly descended sharply, falling over 20,000 feet per minute and slamming into the ground near Greenacres, creating a crater from which smoke was seen rising. Disturbing air traffic control recording reveals how the pilot called out “Mayday” and then said, “We're going to crash into the ground.”

Filgueiras had texted her boyfriend only ten minutes prior to the incident, telling him that she was facing turbulence and icing, as per her stepfather. "I wanted her to fulfil her dream, but I understood very well that her dream was the thing that would make her leave me," her mother said. "I know she was following her dream."

Filgueiras hit the local news headlines in 2023 after she received a pilot's license when she was 17 years old, even before she got her driver's license.

Her education was financed by the School District of Palm Beach County's Aviation Academy. "I definitely do brag because people tell me, 'Oh, you can't drive,' and I say to them, 'Yes, I can drive, but I can fly as well,'" she said in an interview with CBS12.

No identity of the remaining eight victims has been released by the authorities yet. An investigation into the reason behind the crash is being conducted by the FAA and the NTSB.

headline: Ariana Grande shares glimpse into life with Ricky Alvarez amid 'break'
subheadline: The pop icon, 33, shares sweet new photos with her boyfriend, 38
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Ariana Grande is enjoying life away from the spotlight with her boyfriend, Ricky Alvarez.

On Monday, November 2, the pop star shared a photo dump on social media featuring moments with Alvarez, her dogs, and friends. She kept the caption simple, adding a heart and three exclamation points.

Among the snapshots, Grande, 33, and Alvarez, 38, were seen embracing and gazing into each other’s eyes during a walk. Another photo captured the singer planting a gentle kiss on her boyfriend’s forehead. The couple rekindled their romance over the summer after first dating in 2016.

READ MORE: Ariana Grande, Ricky Alvarez level up relationship after matching tattoos

The post also offered a closer look at Grande’s dramatic new haircut. The singer recently traded her signature long locks for a bob.

Away from her romantic life, Grande has also been spending more time with her 10 dogs following the recent loss of Coco, her first-ever pet, who died last month after 17 years together.

The photo dump offers a rare glimpse into Grande’s life since wrapping up her Eternal Sunshine tour on September 1. Before the tour ended, her spokesperson told People magazine that the singer “looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny.”

headline: Pakistan Literature Festival brings writers, poets, scholars from three nations to Houston
subheadline: Discussions cover Urdu literature, Pakistani culture, journalism, cinema and social challenges in a rapidly digitising world
author: Raja Zahid Akhtar Khanazada
article_text:
HOUSTON: The third Pakistan Literature Festival, a two-day event organised by the International Academy of Letters USA, concluded on November 1 in Sugar Land and Stafford, in the Houston area of the US state of Texas.

Held on October 31 and November 1, the festival brought together writers, poets, journalists, intellectuals and artists from Pakistan, the United States and Canada. Discussions covered Urdu language and literature, Pakistani culture, journalism, cinema, television drama, the identity of the younger generation, social issues and challenges facing Pakistan.

Pakistan's Ambassador to the United States, Rizwan Saeed Sheikh, was unable to attend in person because of official commitments but addressed the gathering through a video message. Pakistan's Consul General in Houston, Aftab Chaudhry, also spoke at the event, which was attended by Canadian parliamentarian Sameer Zuberi.

The festival was organised by Ghazanfar Hashmi, president of the International Academy of Letters USA, who welcomed the participants.

The opening day began at the Ismaili Jamatkhana and Centre in Sugar Land with an inaugural ceremony, followed by panel discussions.

A discussion titled "Women's Voices in Urdu Literature" featured Professor Tahira Naqvi, Ishrat Afreen, Dr Saima Iram, Mona Shahab, Bina Goindi and Tasneem Abidi. Nasira Zuberi moderated the session.

Another discussion, "Two Cultures, Two Generations: New Concepts of Leadership", included Dr Mohsin Ansari, Canadian MP Sameer Zuberi, Dr Imran Sharif, Siraj Narsi, Maria Kari and Umar Khawaja. Ibrahim Javed moderated the panel.

Mental health, its challenges and possible solutions were discussed by Nasruddin Rupani, Dr Asim Shah, Dr Mohsin Ansari, Mahtab Muradi, Nusrat Haris and Asif Sinan. Mazhar Khawaja moderated the discussion, while Naveeda Hashmi delivered the opening remarks.

A panel on the past and present of Pakistani cinema and television drama featured Shahab Zuberi, Nilofar Abbasi, Noor Naghmi, Adil Murad, Kamran Ali Asdar and Yasir Raza. Najia Ashar moderated the discussion.

The day's cultural programme also included "Sham-e-Ishq" (An Evening of Love), featuring Sufi music performances by Hasnain Javed and Asif Sinan.

On November 1, the programme moved to the Tuscany Ballroom at the Spark by Hilton in Stafford, where literary and intellectual discussions continued.

A panel titled "Iqbal: A Poet for Every Age" featured Dr Muhammad Naeem Virk, Dr Saima Iram, Atif Tauqeer, Pervez Jafri and other scholars.

The discussion "Pakistani Media: Truth and Responsibility" brought together journalists Shahab Zuberi, Raza Rumi, Ashraf Shad, Fazil Jamili, Faisal Aziz Khan and Khurram Shahzad. Yousuf Chaudhry delivered the opening remarks, while Ghazanfar Hashmi moderated. The panellists discussed journalistic responsibilities, challenges facing the news media and changes in the media landscape.

Another discussion, "Reimagining Pakistan's Future: Challenges and Opportunities", featured Shabbar Zaidi, with Ghazanfar Hashmi and Nasira Zuberi as moderators.

The programme also included activities related to books, fine arts and Pakistan's cultural heritage.

The closing ceremony was followed by an international mushaira, a traditional Urdu poetry gathering, presided over by Khawaja Razi Haider and hosted by Mehboob Zafar. Several poets recited their work.

The festival offered members of the Pakistani diaspora a platform to exchange ideas on literature, language, culture and contemporary issues.

As the two-day gathering drew to a close, a key message emerging from the discussions was the need to pass on the connection to the Urdu language and literature to the next generation and strengthen intellectual and cultural ties.

headline: Dustin Hoffman calls making 'The Graduate' a 'terrible experience'
subheadline: Dustin Hoffman Reveals Mike Nichols’ 'Sadism' On The Graduate Set
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Dustin Hoffman has described the making of The Graduate, the film that earned him his first Oscar nomination, as a miserable experience, laying out a difficult relationship with director Mike Nichols in a new essay for The New Yorker.

“It was a terrible experience making the movie that changed my life,” Hoffman wrote in the piece, which was published over the weekend and is largely focused on his dealings with Nichols.

The actor says Nichols was warm and welcoming during rehearsals, but became a different person once cameras started rolling.

According to Hoffman, the director “was irritable with everyone, but with me a certain sadism seemed to creep in.”

One of the most striking episodes he recalls involves a scene in which co-star Katharine Ross had to slap him.

Nichols reportedly made the pair go through twenty-seven takes, and the moment never made it into the finished film.

The physical toll did not end there.

Hoffman writes that he punctured an eardrum while filming a pool scene in a wetsuit, and that he came close to losing consciousness while shooting the sequence in which his character runs to the church.

Looking back, Hoffman says he came to understand what was going on.

He believes Nichols was using him as a stand-in for his own feelings, particularly in the wake of the director’s split from his former comedy partner Elaine May.

In his words, he was “there to absorb Mike’s own self-loathing.”

The Graduate turned Hoffman, then a relative newcomer, into a household name, and it remains one of the most celebrated American films of its era.

His account of the shoot offers a very different picture of what went on behind the scenes of the 1967 classic.

Hoffman has himself faced allegations of inappropriate behaviour on various sets over the years, including a well-publicised incident involving a slap to Meryl Streep during the making of Kramer vs. Kramer.

headline: What happened at Boca Ciega high school? Everything to know
subheadline: Lockdown lifted at Boca Ciega high school after report of masked, knife-wielding suspects
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A report of people wearing masks with knives at a high school in Gulfport has sent students and parents into a state of panic on Monday after a lockdown was initiated for about two hours.

Around 10:15 am, the Gulfport Police Department received a call from Boca Ciega High School concerning three individuals "wearing ski masks and knives," said GPD. The school was locked down immediately, with the Pinellas County Sheriff's Office, Pinellas County Schools Police, Indian Shores Police Department and local firefighters converging on the location of the crime.

No threat was found by the authorities, but the individual described in the call has been captured by CCTV cameras leaving the school premises. Law enforcement is currently trying to identify the individual.

Fortunately, no one has sustained any injuries. The school was allowed to reopen at 12:22 p.m. After the lockdown ended, parents were informed about the case through a message sent out by the school, according to GPD.

Photos from the scene indicated that there was an increased law enforcement presence on the campus in the morning as the sweeps were carried out. There has been an alarm among the Gulfport community members after the news about the threat to the school reached the parents.

It is unclear whether the threat was real and whether the person who appeared on the surveillance videos had any intentions to cause harm. The investigations are still going on, and the police department has requested everyone who has information to contact them.

The lockdown happens against the backdrop of the current concerns regarding school security in Florida and in the country.

headline: Cyberattacks leave supermarket freezers warm, food stocks destroyed across Europe
subheadline: Belgian SPAR stores and Carrefour marts also affected; latest attack comes weeks after similar hack in France last month
author: Reuters
article_text:
Delhaize stores hit by 'IT incident' in Belgium, Luxembourg
Sweden's national cybersecurity centre probing incidents.
ICA store in Sweden says refrigerators hit by cyber attack.

A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.

The attack, which raised temperatures in refrigerator and freezer units at dozens of stores, hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer IKEA also saw at least one store affected.

"Everything is destroyed," Engla Ingwall, sales manager at an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, told Reuters during a visit to the store on Monday, adding the attack occurred at 2 a.m. (0100 GMT) but was only noticed hours later.

"There has been a cyberattack and all our freezers reached 50 degrees (Celsius)."

A spokesperson for privately held ICA said the company was aware that a "limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems".

The latest incidents follow an attack in France last month when police said hackers seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses. Ahold also reported a cybersecurity incident to police last month.

While no one has claimed responsibility for either attack, the incidents have heightened concerns among European authorities about hybrid threats to infrastructure amid growing security tensions since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Moscow has repeatedly denied involvement in sabotage or hybrid warfare operations. Reuters could not establish who was behind Monday's attacks or whether they were linked to the incidents in France.

"It is not known who is behind this attack, and it may never be determined," said Katrien Eggers, spokesperson for Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity, adding she was concerned about the growing number of incidents, in part due to AI.

"All IT systems are potentially vulnerable, and AI can now be used to successfully exploit these weaknesses — especially by sophisticated actors," she said.

'Retail is an easy target'

From refrigerators and heating systems to security cameras and alarms, an expanding range of devices once largely mechanical can now be monitored and controlled remotely, creating new opportunities for cybercriminals.

At least some of the refrigerator units affected on Monday used temperature control technology from Danish firm Danfoss that was also targeted in the French attack. The firm said it had been working with customers to implement fixes.

The European Commission said the latest incidents highlighted how digital threats are becoming increasingly disruptive.

"They are a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain and undermine consumers' confidence in it – a warning that we must take seriously," said EU commissioner for agriculture Christophe Hansen. "The repeated occurrence of these cyberattacks is deeply concerning."

A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, said five shops had their fridge systems attacked.

In Ireland, wholesaler Musgrave said the incident affected systems in 13 of its SuperValu stores, forcing it to remove some chilled and frozen products from sale.

"Our monitoring systems alerted us to the issue and we took immediate action," it said in a statement. "Our investigation is ongoing."

Tom Hegel, a researcher at cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, said such attacks were typically linked to extortion, political motives or nation-state operations, with the absence of financial demands in recent cases pointing instead to sabotage.

"Retail is an easy target because retail chains run enormous estates of refrigeration controllers, building management systems, door access panels and point-of-sale gear," he said, adding it was hard to trace hackers targeting such systems.

"An attacker who logs into an exposed control panel leaves almost nothing behind ... A teenager and an intelligence service would look much the same from the defender's side."

'It's very scary'

Carrefour, which was badly hit in last month's French attack, said 15 of its 700 stores in Belgium were affected. IKEA said one store in Belgium had been impacted and that it could not rule out disruptions at other locations.

Privately held Swedish grocery chain Coop said that 7 of its 800 stores were affected by a cyber incident involving unauthorised tampering with its refrigeration systems. It said Danfoss was among its suppliers.

Luc De Laet, founder and owner of Belgian butchery chain De Laet & Van Haver, said he was woken at 3:30 a.m. by an employee telling him there was a problem. He rushed to his store south of Antwerp and found the fridges turned up as high as 18 C.

He estimated the incident ruined about €15,000 ($16,800) worth of meat.

"It's very scary. They are hacking the system that is doing the registration of the temperature, and they can program it at a distance," he told Reuters, adding that it was infuriating to throw away so much food.

De Laet said he believed the hackers were trying to destabilise European economies. He had contacted police but did not know whether an investigation had been launched.

"I only have two words for them: wake up, please, because there's something going on," he said.

• Delhaize stores hit by 'IT incident' in Belgium, Luxembourg
  • Sweden's national cybersecurity centre probing incidents.
  • ICA store in Sweden says refrigerators hit by cyber attack.

A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.

The attack, which raised temperatures in refrigerator and freezer units at dozens of stores, hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer IKEA also saw at least one store affected.

"Everything is destroyed," Engla Ingwall, sales manager at an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, told Reuters during a visit to the store on Monday, adding the attack occurred at 2 a.m. (0100 GMT) but was only noticed hours later.

"There has been a cyberattack and all our freezers reached 50 degrees (Celsius)."

A spokesperson for privately held ICA said the company was aware that a "limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems".

The latest incidents follow an attack in France last month when police said hackers seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses. Ahold also reported a cybersecurity incident to police last month.

While no one has claimed responsibility for either attack, the incidents have heightened concerns among European authorities about hybrid threats to infrastructure amid growing security tensions since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Moscow has repeatedly denied involvement in sabotage or hybrid warfare operations. Reuters could not establish who was behind Monday's attacks or whether they were linked to the incidents in France.

"It is not known who is behind this attack, and it may never be determined," said Katrien Eggers, spokesperson for Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity, adding she was concerned about the growing number of incidents, in part due to AI.

"All IT systems are potentially vulnerable, and AI can now be used to successfully exploit these weaknesses — especially by sophisticated actors," she said.

'Retail is an easy target'

From refrigerators and heating systems to security cameras and alarms, an expanding range of devices once largely mechanical can now be monitored and controlled remotely, creating new opportunities for cybercriminals.

At least some of the refrigerator units affected on Monday used temperature control technology from Danish firm Danfoss that was also targeted in the French attack. The firm said it had been working with customers to implement fixes.

The European Commission said the latest incidents highlighted how digital threats are becoming increasingly disruptive.

"They are a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain and undermine consumers' confidence in it – a warning that we must take seriously," said EU commissioner for agriculture Christophe Hansen. "The repeated occurrence of these cyberattacks is deeply concerning."

A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, said five shops had their fridge systems attacked.

In Ireland, wholesaler Musgrave said the incident affected systems in 13 of its SuperValu stores, forcing it to remove some chilled and frozen products from sale.

"Our monitoring systems alerted us to the issue and we took immediate action," it said in a statement. "Our investigation is ongoing."

Tom Hegel, a researcher at cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, said such attacks were typically linked to extortion, political motives or nation-state operations, with the absence of financial demands in recent cases pointing instead to sabotage.

"Retail is an easy target because retail chains run enormous estates of refrigeration controllers, building management systems, door access panels and point-of-sale gear," he said, adding it was hard to trace hackers targeting such systems.

"An attacker who logs into an exposed control panel leaves almost nothing behind ... A teenager and an intelligence service would look much the same from the defender's side."

'It's very scary'

Carrefour, which was badly hit in last month's French attack, said 15 of its 700 stores in Belgium were affected. IKEA said one store in Belgium had been impacted and that it could not rule out disruptions at other locations.

Privately held Swedish grocery chain Coop said that 7 of its 800 stores were affected by a cyber incident involving unauthorised tampering with its refrigeration systems. It said Danfoss was among its suppliers.

Luc De Laet, founder and owner of Belgian butchery chain De Laet & Van Haver, said he was woken at 3:30 a.m. by an employee telling him there was a problem. He rushed to his store south of Antwerp and found the fridges turned up as high as 18 C.

He estimated the incident ruined about €15,000 ($16,800) worth of meat.

"It's very scary. They are hacking the system that is doing the registration of the temperature, and they can program it at a distance," he told Reuters, adding that it was infuriating to throw away so much food.

De Laet said he believed the hackers were trying to destabilise European economies. He had contacted police but did not know whether an investigation had been launched.

"I only have two words for them: wake up, please, because there's something going on," he said.

headline: Ben Wang reportedly circling major role In Marvel's X-Men reboot
subheadline: X-Men Reboot: Ben Wang tapped by Marvel Studios
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping actor Ben Wang is reportedly in the frame to play Iceman in Marvel Studios’ upcoming X-Men reboot.

Deadline reports that he is circling the role of Bobby Drake and is the studio’s top choice.

Marvel has not officially announced his involvement, so the casting remains unconfirmed.

Read more: Jennifer Lawrence rules out her probablity of returning to 'X-Men'

The outlet says other young actors have also tested for the part, including Gabriel LaBelle, Jackson Kelly and Rhenzy Feliz.

Wang is best known for starring in the TV series American Born Chinese and for his role in Karate Kid: Legends.

He also appeared in The Long Walk, and he will next be seen in the Hunger Games prequel, in which he plays Wyatt Callow.

If the deal comes together, he would join a growing line-up for the film.

Kit Connor has been cast as Cyclops and Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, with Inde Navarrette playing Rogue, Asa Germann as Angel and Maya Boyd, making her feature debut, as Storm.

Christopher Abbott is set to play Professor Xavier, Samara Weaving will appear as Emma Frost and Adam Driver is reported to be playing Mister Sinister.

The reboot is being directed by Jake Schreier, with Joanna Calo, Lee Sung Jin and Michael Lesslie among the writers.

Kevin Feige is producing, and the film is currently slated to arrive in cinemas on 5 May 2028.

Iceman has long been one of the best-known members of the original X-Men team, and the character’s casting is likely to be closely watched by fans as Marvel builds a new generation of mutants for the big screen.

Read more: Famke Janssen wants ‘Backrooms' filmmaker to direct an ‘X-Men' film

headline: Trump's record low approval rating puts Republicans on defensive ahead of midterms
subheadline: Latest Reuters/Ipsos survey shows 49% of Democratic voters very enthusiastic about voting, compared with 33% of Republicans
author: Reuters
article_text:
Trump job approval stands at 32%, near record low.
Half of independents see Tuesday's vote as opposition to Trump.
Voters favour Democrats by 46% to 38% on generic congressional ballot.

President Donald Trump's approval rating held near a career low as a broad swath of the US electorate saw their vote in Tuesday's congressional midterm elections as a way to oppose the Republican president, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday.

The poll results underscore Republican vulnerabilities brought on by a surge in fuel prices since Trump launched a war on Iran in February. Voters in the nationwide poll said they preferred Democrats over Republicans — 46% to 38% — in what is known as a "generic ballot" question.

Still, that 8-percentage-point Democratic advantage was narrower than in a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted a week earlier, when Democrats led by 11 points.

The generic ballot question gives an overall view of which party voters nationwide would like to see in charge in Congress, though it does not capture the nuances of the state-by-state and district-by-district contests that determine control of the US Senate and US ‌House of Representatives.

Trump's fellow Republicans are fighting to retain the party's majorities in Congress.

Political strategists from both parties think Democrats have the best shot at winning control of the House, where all 435 seats are up for grabs. Democrats face a more difficult path to victory in the US Senate, with the party on the defensive in Alaska and Michigan in recent days.

While Trump won't be on the ballot, he looms large in the election.

Some 32% of poll respondents said they approved of the job Trump was doing in the White House, unchanged from a week earlier and just above his record-low reading of 31% two weeks ago.

Among registered voters, some 50% of independents said they saw their vote in congressional elections as a vote against Trump, compared with 13% who said it was a vote for Trump and 33% who said the president wasn't a factor in their vote.

Some 78% of voters said the rising cost of living would be very important or the most important issue in deciding how to vote. Asked which party was better on the issue, voters in the poll picked Democrats over Republicans, 43% to 32%.

Democrats appear to have more enthusiasm about voting, which the party hopes will lead to an advantage in voter turnout. Some 49% of Democratic voters said they are "very enthusiastic" about voting this year, compared with 33% of Republicans.

The latest Reuters/Ipsos poll surveyed 1,765 US adults online and had a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

headline: US to host renewed Ukraine-Russia peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11, says Witkoff
subheadline: Discussions expected to cover ending the war, post-war security agreements, de-escalation and humanitarian measures
author: Reuters
article_text:
The United States will bring together delegations from Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 for fresh talks aimed at ending Moscow's war against Kyiv, with discussions expected to cover post-war security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian measures, US envoy Steve Witkoff said on Monday.

The latest diplomatic push comes as Washington seeks to revive negotiations before winter sets in, with the conflict continuing to inflict heavy damage on Ukraine and showing little sign of a military resolution.

Witkoff, announcing the planned discussions in a social media post, said the agenda would include "post-war security agreements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures, and ending the war".

Witkoff and Jared Kushner, US President Donald Trump's son-in-law and a lead negotiator in the peace efforts, are expected to represent Washington at the Abu Dhabi meetings, a senior US official told Reuters.

Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to a fresh round of trilateral negotiations following a meeting with Witkoff in St Petersburg two weeks ago, marking a renewed attempt by the Trump administration to bring Moscow and Kyiv back to the negotiating table.

Ahead of the talks, US negotiators will hold working-level discussions in Brussels this week with representatives from France, Germany, Britain, the European Union and Nato.

The meetings will focus on security guarantees for Ukraine, Europe's future security framework and financial support for Ukraine's reconstruction, the US official said.

The discussions are intended to build on recent diplomatic contacts and reflect Trump's efforts to secure a lasting settlement between the two countries.

Deep divisions over peace terms

Despite renewed diplomatic activity, Moscow and Kyiv remain sharply divided over the terms of any potential settlement, particularly territorial control and security arrangements for Ukraine after the war.

Russia has maintained demands for Ukraine to relinquish territory it claims to have annexed, while Kyiv has rejected territorial concessions and sought firm security guarantees to deter any future Russian attack.

Ukraine has also pushed for assurances from Western allies, including potential European-led security arrangements and continued military support. The precise form of any post-war guarantees remains unresolved.

The territorial dispute has been a central obstacle in previous rounds of negotiations. Moscow has also sought restrictions on Ukraine's military capabilities and its future relationship with Nato, positions that Kyiv has resisted.

The last formal US-mediated trilateral peace talks took place in February, with further negotiations disrupted after the United States and Israel launched their war against Iran later that month.

US envoys Witkoff and Kushner renewed diplomatic contacts with Moscow and Kyiv in September, although those discussions did not produce a breakthrough. The proposed Abu Dhabi meeting would bring the three sides together again in a trilateral format.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. The conflict has since become Europe's largest war since World War Two, with repeated diplomatic efforts failing to resolve fundamental disagreements over territory, sovereignty and security.

The upcoming talks will test whether the renewed US-led initiative can narrow those differences and establish a framework for ending the fighting.

Russia has maintained demands for Ukraine to relinquish territory it claims to have annexed, while Kyiv has rejected territorial concessions and sought firm security guarantees to deter any future Russian attack.

Ukraine has also pushed for assurances from Western allies, including potential European-led security arrangements and continued military support. The precise form of any post-war guarantees remains unresolved.

The territorial dispute has been a central obstacle in previous rounds of negotiations. Moscow has also sought restrictions on Ukraine's military capabilities and its future relationship with Nato, positions that Kyiv has resisted.
The last formal US-mediated trilateral peace talks took place in February, with further negotiations disrupted after the United States and Israel launched their war against Iran later that month.

US envoys Witkoff and Kushner renewed diplomatic contacts with Moscow and Kyiv in September, although those discussions did not produce a breakthrough. The proposed Abu Dhabi meeting would bring the three sides together again in a trilateral format.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. The conflict has since become Europe's largest war since World War Two, with repeated diplomatic efforts failing to resolve fundamental disagreements over territory, sovereignty and security.
The upcoming talks will test whether the renewed US-led initiative can narrow those differences and establish a framework for ending the fighting.

headline: King Charles reveals his softer side in new video from garden visit
subheadline: King Charles learns about Guyana’s painful past in Georgetown
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles took a moment to stop and admire one of nature’s delicate displays during his visit to Guyana.

King Charles paused to smell a beautiful water lily at the historic Promenade Gardens in Georgetown.

A video shared by the royal family channel showed the King appeared captivated by the flower as he explored one of the city’s oldest public gardens.

Read More: King Charles office shares first post after monarch's angry outburst

During the engagement, King Charles met Carlos Magdalena, a botanical horticulturist from the Royal Botanic Gardens, and spent time with members of the National Piping Centre alongside Guyanese drummers.

The monarch later shared a light-hearted exchange with schoolchildren gathered to see him.

Joking about their attendance, he asked: “I hope they have given you the day off school to be here! Are they giving you a lot of homework instead?”

He also explored an urban park in Georgetown, where he was given a review of Guyana’s history.

At the entrance, formerly known as the Parade Ground, local historian Mr Jacobs briefed the King on the site’s past.

Charles also paused before a memorial plaque commemorating enslaved people who were sentenced to death and hanged at the site following the 1823 rebellion.

headline: Lake Bell, Rashid Johnson go red carpet official at 2026 CFDA awards
subheadline: Lake Bell, Rashid Johnson attend CFDA awards after Instagram hard launch
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Lake Bell and her boyfriend, the artist Rashid Johnson, have made their red carpet debut as a couple at the 2026 CFDA Awards, just days after confirming their relationship on Instagram.

The appearance follows a Halloween “hard launch” that got fans talking.

On Saturday 31 October, the Boston Legal actress, 47, shared a photo of herself in a black stole and matching beret, with Johnson, 49, beside her in a navy velvet tuxedo jacket.

Read more: Lake Bell and Rashid Johnson go Instagram official on Halloween

She captioned it “Happy Hallow-hard launch.”

The pair had already been seen out together in recent weeks.

They attended a New York Times event in September marking 175 years of independent reporting, and a few days before their Instagram post they were at the American Ballet Theatre Fall Gala.

It is not known how long they have been together.

Bell was married to the tattoo artist Scott Campbell from 2013 to 2020, and the former couple share two children, Nova, 12, and Ozgood, 9. She was also reported to be dating Chris Rock in 2022.

Johnson, one of the leading artists of his generation, was married for 15 years to the artist Sheree Hovsepian.

The couple announced their split earlier this year and have a 14-year-old son, Julius.

With the CFDA Awards appearance following so soon after the Instagram post, the couple appear comfortable being seen together in public.

The event is one of the biggest nights in the American fashion calendar, which makes it a high-profile place to step out for the first time on a red carpet.

headline: Duchess Sophie reveals Queen's delight over powerful Commonwealth legacy
subheadline: Duchess Sophie’s whirlwind trip to Antigua revealed with details of preventing blindess
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Duchess of Edinburgh made a brief visit to Antigua and Barbuda before returning to the UK.

Sophie travelled to the Caribbean nation as Global Ambassador for the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness (IAPB), devoted to improving access to eye care avoidable sight loss.

Her first engagement took her to a new primary eye care unit at the Magistrates Court in St John’s, where she was welcomed by the Cure Blindness Project ahead of the Global Summit for Eye Health.

Read More: Duchess Sophie embraces earthy tones for colourful Victoria Falls adventure

During the visit, the Duchess met patients whose sight had recently been restored, hearing first-hand how treatment had transformed their lives.

She also spoke with nurses, ophthalmologists and other healthcare professionals working to make eye care more accessible across Antigua and Barbuda.

The visit held particular significance for Sophie, who has spent more than 20 years supporting international efforts to prevent avoidable blindness.

Later, she attended the Global Summit for Eye Health at the John E St Luce Conference Centre, where she delivered a keynote address calling for greater action to tackle preventable blindness.

In her speech, Sophie thanked the Government of Antigua and Barbuda for hosting the gathering, alongside its co-hosting nations Bangladesh, Guyana, Nigeria and Ireland.

She said: “The treatment of avoidable blindness is as imperative as any other health challenge, not only because it prevents individuals from losing their window onto the world, curtailing life chances and choices, but if treated with low-cost and effective interventions, there huge returns to be had.

“I've been involved in eye health for more than 20 years in my role as Global Ambassador for Vision 2020 and the IAPB.

I also had the honour to serve as Vice Patron of the Queen Elizabeth Diamond Jubilee Trust, set up to honour Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth in 2012, and with its principal mission of tackling avoidable blindness across the Commonwealth.

“Over the decades, I have visited eye care programmes in many countries, including Africa, Asia, South America, and beyond.

And in fact, this morning I was at one of the very clinics that Prime Minister Browne was actually just describing, two already set up and two in train, and met with some of the healthcare professionals, the nurses who in fact went to India for their training and have recently returned, and they're already up and running and making an impact.

“I've seen the overwhelming joy when the bandages are removed after cataract surgery and sight loss, even after decades, is restored.

“I've witnessed trachoma operations which not only save sight but deliver those afflicted from a lifetime of agonising pain and discomfort.”

According to the Court Circular, her visit concluded after the summit, with the Duchess flying back to the UK.

headline: McKenna Grace reveals one 'terrifying' thing she won't do on-screen
subheadline: McKenna Grace opens up about boundaries on-screen ahead of 'Hunger Games'
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Hunger Games star McKenna Grace has said she does not take on roles that involve explicit scenes, describing the prospect as “terrifying”.

The 20-year-old actress made the comments in an interview with Cosmopolitan, speaking ahead of the release of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

“At this point, I definitely don’t do nudity or very hypersexual things,” she said. She added: “I respect anybody who can, but it’s terrifying to me. I don’t know if that’ll ever change.”

Read more: 'Hunger Games' reveals massive surprise in 'SOTR' tracklist

Grace was keen to make clear that this does not mean she sticks to wholesome projects. She pointed to her role in Scream, where her character is killed by Ghostface, as proof that her work can be dark.

She also spoke about her ambition to play a Disney princess one day.

The star’s next big release is the Hunger Games prequel, which focuses on Haymitch Abernathy and arrives in cinemas on 20 November.

She plays Maysilee Donner, a District 12 tribute in the Second Quarter Quell. Grace is a longtime fan of the franchise, and has spoken about making “Team Peeta” edits as a teenager.

Having started out as a child actress, Grace has built a career that spans Gifted, I, Tonya and Regretting You, as well as TV roles in The Handmaid’s Tale, The Haunting of Hill House and Chilling Adventures of Sabrina.

Read more: Mckenna Grace opens up about vulnerability in being 'loud' about love life

headline: Ellen DeGeneres emotional after sudden death of producer Matthew Wright
subheadline: Ellen DeGeneres breaks down in tears in tribute to producer Matthew Wright
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Ellen DeGeneres has broken down in tears in a video tribute to her longtime producer Matthew Wright, who has died suddenly at the age of 52.

The former talk show host, 68, shared a selfie video on Monday 2 November, captioned with a broken-heart emoji. It included a montage of Wright’s sketches from The Ellen DeGeneres Show.

“Everyone loved him,” she said, describing the news as “shocking, it’s just shocking.”

Struggling for words, she said: “I don’t know what I’m saying.” She added: “I’m so sorry, ’cause we lost a good guy.”

DeGeneres also revealed that she and Wright had only just begun working on a new project together.

Wright died on Friday 30 October. His family described the loss as an “unfathomable tragedy” on a GoFundMe page, and the cause of death has not been released.

He worked on The Ellen DeGeneres Show for 16 years, until it ended in 2022.

At the time, he wrote: “How do I even begin to sum jup 16 years of my life?” He also thanked the show for “taking a chance on me and changing my life!”

The fundraiser says Wright and his husband, Justin, were both laid off this summer, and that the family cannot afford the costs of bringing him home, a funeral and a memorial.

The goal is $50,000, and about half had been raised by Monday.

Former colleague Andy Lassner has also paid tribute on Instagram. He said he saw Wright only hours before his death, when he visited him on the set of The Jennifer Hudson Show.

“We are all in shock,” Lassner wrote, calling Wright “a brilliant producer and an even better human being.”

headline: Queen Camilla makes strong statement on women's safety, brushing off soggy hair
subheadline: Queen Camilla enjoys a moment with locals over African game
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Queen Camilla has once again made her support for women impossible to miss, meeting survivors of abuse and campaigners fighting for greater protection across the Commonwealth.

On Monday, the Queen joined the Commonwealth Women’s Forum, where she listened to those affected by abuse and engaged with political leaders.

Buckingham Palace revealed that Camilla also met women who are working to improve the lives of others.

Read More: Queen Camilla makes Caribbean return in vibrant turquoise joining King Charles

During her address at the Forum, the Queen spoke about encouraging signs of progress in the fight to protect women.

“Throughout our Commonwealth, people are identifying effective ways to ensure that, when a woman reaches out for help, she finds it close at hand,” she said.

Away from the discussions, she also took an interest in a very different part of the region’s heritage when she met locals playing Warri, a traditional board game regarded as one of the oldest in the world, with roots in Africa.

The game carries a deeper historical significance beyond its strategy and competition.

During the era of slavery, it provided enslaved men with an important social space in which they could maintain connections to African culture and traditions.

The Commonwealth also used the occasion to underline the wider purpose of the gathering, sharing a message on X: “Everyone must be part of the solution.”

The opening of the Forum brought together governments, civil society groups, development partners and young people, with discussions centred on equality, safety and opportunity for women and girls.

Speaking at the event, Deputy Secretary-General (Corporate) Tania Baumann urged delegates to ensure that women and girls have greater opportunities to participate, contribute and thrive.

She challenged attendees to leave the gathering with “clear, practical commitments” that would translate into greater safety, opportunity and control over their futures.

headline: Neve Campbell confirms return in 'Scream 8'
subheadline: Neve Campbell confirms 'Scream 8' return, teasing 'that’s in the pipeline'
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Neve Campbell has confirmed that she will return as Sidney Prescott in Scream 8, less than a year after Scream 7 became the highest-grossing film in the franchise.

The actress made the announcement on Monday during an Associated Press interview promoting her Netflix series Black Doves.

Asked about the horror franchise, she said: “Scream 8. That’s in the pipeline as well.”

Read more: Neve Campbell turned down ‘Scream 6' - Here's why

Pressed on what the character will face next, Campbell laughed and refused to give anything away. “You know I can’t tell you anything about Scream 8,” she said. “I’ll be in it.”

Her confirmation comes on the back of a huge success for the series.

Scream 7 opened in 2025 with the biggest debut in the franchise’s history, taking $97.2 million worldwide in its first weekend.

It went on to earn $208 million globally from a $45 million budget, making it the most successful film in the saga so far.

Spyglass Media and Paramount Pictures, which distributes the series, began developing a follow-up soon afterwards.

Campbell’s relationship with the franchise has not always been smooth.

She sat out Scream 6 in 2023 because of a contract dispute, leaving the film without the character who has been at the heart of the series since Wes Craven’s original.

She came back for Scream 7 after a reported $7 million salary.

Her latest comments suggest the partnership is firmly back on track. Sidney Prescott remains one of horror’s most recognisable final girls, and with the last film’s box office numbers, the studio has every reason to keep the character at the centre of the next chapter.

headline: Johnny Depp reveals what it would take to bring him back as Jack Sparrow
subheadline: Johnny Depp says he would work with Jerry Bruckheimer
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Johnny Depp has said he is open to returning as Captain Jack Sparrow in a new Pirates of the Caribbean film, as long as it gives the franchise the ending he feels it deserves.

The actor spoke to Entertainment Tonight during the press tour for his holiday film Ebenezer.

He has not confirmed that he has signed on, but he made clear that his motivation would be to help the series finish strongly and “send them off on a better note.”

Read more: Johnny Depp in talks to return as Jack Sparrow for 'Pirates of the Caribbean 6'

Depp also said he would be ready to work with producer Jerry Bruckheimer at very short notice.

Bruckheimer has been equally positive about the idea.

In 2025, he told Entertainment Weekly that he had spoken to Depp and felt good about the chances, provided the actor liked how the role was written.

He has described the project as a reboot, but has said Depp would be part of it if it were up to him, since Depp created the character.

At D23 in August 2026, the producer said talks with Depp were ongoing and that the screenplay was still in development.

Geoffrey Rush has also discussed a possible return as Barbossa, though Disney has not announced a cast or a release date for the next film.

Depp played Jack Sparrow in all five films, from The Curse of the Black Pearl in 2003 to Dead Men Tell No Tales in 2017.

Disney moved on from him in 2018, and during his 2022 defamation trial he testified that he would not go back to the role for any amount of money.

His latest comments mark a clear shift in tone, and fans of the swashbuckling series will be watching to see whether the talks turn into a deal.

Read more: Johnny Depp's casting in 'Pirates of the Caribbean 6' addressed in new statement

headline: Candice Swanepoel reveals where things stand with Tom Brady
subheadline: Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel prefer dates whenever their schedules allow
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel may be enjoying their new romance, but wedding bells aren't ringing just yet.

Despite fresh engagement speculation after the Victoria’s Secret model was spotted wearing a gold band on her left ring finger on October 30, a source close to Swanepoel tells People magazine that she is not engaged to the retired NFL quarterback.

And it sounds like neither is in a hurry to turn their relationship into something more serious.

Read More: Candice Swanepoel spotted with gold ring as Tom Brady romance heats up

“She likes spending time with him. Between her kids and her career, her plate is very full. Tom’s independent and has a busy life too, which works well for her,” the source said.

“They go on dates when they can and have fun together. It’s not a super intense relationship. They both have a lot going on and are happy to see each other when their schedules allow,” the insider added.

The pair's romance was confirmed by the outlet on October 25, after they reportedly met through mutual friends in Miami earlier this summer.

“They’d been running in the same circle,” another source said, adding that Brady is attentive and makes an effort to make their time together special.

Both stars also understand the juggling act of parenting. Brady shares three children with exes Bridget Moynahan and Gisele Bündchen, while Swanepoel has two sons with her former fiancé Hermann Nicoli.

Brady previously admitted that dating can be tricky with his packed schedule.

Read More: Tom Brady's romance with Candice Swanepoel gets fresh details

“You know what? I don’t have much time for a personal life or much time for myself, but I love working, and I love my kids,” he told the outlet.

So, for now, it seems the couple are happy keeping things uncomplicated.
